new_statements.rule_in_words: No placement rule is recoverable. What is visible: Rensch treats the ballistic/controlled opposition as a property of stressed syllables ('In Chinantec it occurs only in stressed syllables'; Amuzgo has it in stressed or unstressed syllables), independent of vowel length in Lalana, with tone allophony described for 'controlled stressed syllables'. new_statements.relation_note: The language is not in the catalog; the only existing statement is an empty pointer to Rensch 1978 Table 28. Mugele 1982 supplies the actual content: it adopts Rensch's (1978) term 'stressed syllable' = Full (stem) syllable, states the Full/Restricted distribution (stem vs affix; final syllable of disyllabic stems), and confines the ballistic/controlled contrast to stressed syllables. Compatible with Rensch 1978 (which Mugele cites as the source of the usage) and with the outside summaries logged earlier (Yip 2002 'stress is on the final syllable'; Oxford Handbook Table 28.6 'controlled stress / ballistic stress' from Mugele 1982:9).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Lalana Chinantec is a tone language (7 tones plus a ballistic/controlled syllable contrast). Word stress is not an independent lexical contrast: the 'stressed syllable' is the Full syllable, which is the stem syllable of the word; affixes, clitics and particles are Restricted (unstressed) syllables with reduced inventories (no long vowels, no nasal contrast, no clusters, no ballistic syllables, no coda /n/, fewer vowels and tones). Stems are almost all monosyllabic; in the rare disyllabic stems the final syllable is the Full (stressed) one. Prefix strings before the stem are unstressed (sec. 4.3.4: 'a sequence of unstressed syllables that precede a stressed syllable'; tone harmony applies only in these). Ch. 4 n. 2: 'ballistic syllables never occur in unstressed syllables.' Historically (p. 145) 'The disyllabic stems of POM were evidently stressed on the second syllable.' Net effect: stress on the stem syllable, which is word-final relative to prefixes (Yip 2002's summary 'stress is on the final syllable' is a restatement of this).
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described. Mugele notes (p. 10-11, quoting Merrifield 1963:15) that the ballistic/controlled contrast could alternatively have been described as primary vs secondary stress, and (ch. 6 n. 2) that Merrifield's 'stress' means ballistic vs controlled; Mugele himself treats ballistic quality as a syllable feature within stressed (Full) syllables, not as a stress degree.
new_statements.exceptions: Rare disyllabic stems: first syllable Restricted, final syllable Full. Some apparent prefixes may be reduced stems in compounds, 'phonologically reduced when not in the stressed syllable' (p. 122). Ballistic/controlled contrast is restricted to Full syllables bearing High, Low or Falling tone and absent in glottal-stop-checked syllables (p. 9).
new_statements.identity_note: Mugele 1982 describes Lalana Chinantec (LC) as spoken in the municipio of San Juan Lalana, Oaxaca (SIL fieldwork tradition of Rensch); no sub-dialect distinguished. Comparative remarks on Palantla, Tepetotutla, etc. and on Proto-Chinantec/Proto-Otomanguean (p. 145) are about other varieties/stages and were not used for the reading.

tone_statements.quote: [p. 73, sec. 3.1.1] El chinanteco de Lalana distingue 13 tonos por sílaba /1 2 2(4) 3 4 12 14 23 21 31 312 42 423/, y sílaba sin especificación tonal /Ø/. En esta escala numérica, el /Ø/ y el /1/ son los tonos más bajos y el /4/ el más alto, y las secuencias de números son tonos de contorno. ... [p. 92, sec. 3.1.3.3] el chinanteco de Lalana presenta poca evidencia en favor a postular alineamiento moraico, por tanto, analizo la sílaba como la UPT. ... [p. 62, sec. 2.4.1] El acento en el léxico nativo se halla en la última sílaba de la palabra que corresponde a la última (y a menudo única) sílaba de la raíz léxica. ... la asignación de acento es demarcativa, y no es léxicamente contrastiva.
tone_statements.translation: [p. 73] Lalana Chinantec distinguishes 13 tones per syllable /1 2 2(4) 3 4 12 14 23 21 31 312 42 423/, plus the syllable without tonal specification /Ø/. On this numerical scale /Ø/ and /1/ are the lowest tones and /4/ the highest, and digit sequences are contour tones. ... [p. 92] Lalana Chinantec offers little evidence for positing moraic alignment, so I analyse the syllable as the tone-bearing unit. ... [p. 62] Stress in the native lexicon lies on the last syllable of the word, which corresponds to the last (and often only) syllable of the lexical root. ... stress assignment is demarcative and not lexically contrastive.

tone_statements.quote: For Lalana Chinantec, Rensch and Rensch state (1966, 457): “There are three contrastive 2itch levels: ‘igh (1), mid (2), and low (3). Either a single tone or a sequence of two or three tones may occur on any syllable regardless of the length of the syllable nucleus." Rensch and Rensch list eight vowels and a length phoneme (462). Thus, there are two possible lengths in the syllable nucleus: vowel, and vowel plus length, and either may take from one to three tones.
tone_statements.locator: p. 26, section 'On the Segmental Nature of Tone' (pp. 24-28)
tone_statements.summary: Three contrastive level tones, high (1), mid (2), low (3); one to three tones in sequence may fall on any syllable, short or long; relayed from Rensch & Rensch 1966, no forms cited.

sources.note: Comparative only. Proto-Chinantec prosodic elements are two tones *H, *L (combinations HL, LH, HLH) and a 'ballistic accent' that 'could occur with both tones and all three combinations' (p. 12); Lalana (Ll) is said to have lost length in accented syllables closed by *? (p. 13). No statement on word-stress placement in any daughter language. downloaded from an Internet Archive copy of the SIL file (SIL file host could not be reached by automated download here).

sources.citation: Mugele, Robert L. 1976. Lalana Chinantec y-. Why? Work Papers of the Summer Institute of Linguistics, University of North Dakota Session 20, Article 3, pp. 1-38. DOI 10.31356/silwp.vol20.03
sources.note: Silent on stress. Morphophonemics of verb stems (vowel shifts, palatalization). Note 2 (p. 37) restates the Rensch & Rensch 1966 phoneme inventory: prosody phonemes = vowel length, vowel nasalization, tone (1 high, 2 mid, 3 low), plus post-vocalic h reanalysed as the prosodic feature 'ballistic syllable' (marked by acute accent); stress is not mentioned anywhere in the 38 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent scanned for stress/accent/prominence).

tone.translation: [it] uses tones to distinguish lexical entries and grammatical functions … The tone system of Eastern Chinantec has two characteristics: on the one hand, some phonological contrasts are limited to the final syllable of a word (cf. Mugele 1982: 9-10); on the other, this variety has the process of tone sandhi … I will analyse the lowest tone as the unmarked tone (/Ø/ henceforth). … the contrast between /1/ and /Ø/, which are phonetically similar, and the floating tone /(4)/.

sources.note: Comparative study of Chinantec phonation: says all Chinantec varieties have three to five basic tones plus melodic tones; Lalana forms carry tone numbers (1 = high) but no Lalana inventory is given.

tone.quote: La racine lexicale est monosyllabique C(G)V(V)3 avec une possibilité de ʔ en coda, ou dans certaines langues s/n/ŋ. Sur ce gabarit restreint se joue un éventail d’articulations secondaires : toutes les variétés ont entre trois et cinq tons basiques avec des tons mélodiques,4 la nasalisation et la phonation non-modale. … Je rapporte les tons tel qu’ils sont donnés le peu de fois où un ton a été noté. Le ton haut est noté 1. Certaines variétés ont jusqu’à quatre tons basiques (I-Ojitlán, V-Quiotepec) et même cinq (I-Usila).
tone.locator: sec. 1.1.1 'Quelques traits phonologiques des langues Ch' + note 6; no printed pagination in the HAL deposit
tone.translation: The lexical root is monosyllabic C(G)V(V) with a possible ʔ coda, or in some languages s/n/ŋ. On this restricted template plays a range of secondary articulations: all the varieties have between three and five basic tones with melodic tones, nasalization and non-modal phonation. … I report the tones as they are given, the few times a tone was noted. High tone is written 1. Some varieties have up to four basic tones (I-Ojitlán, V-Quiotepec) and even five (I-Usila).
tone.summary: Comparative study of Chinantec phonation: says all Chinantec varieties have three to five basic tones plus melodic tones; Lalana forms carry tone numbers (1 = high) but no Lalana inventory is given.
tone.says: Comparative study of Chinantec phonation: says all Chinantec varieties have three to five basic tones plus melodic tones; Lalana forms carry tone numbers (1 = high) but no Lalana inventory is given.
